stepGender.title: Life Expectancy
stepGender.description: How long your retirement fund needs to last depends on your lifespan. Based on Taiwan's Ministry of Interior 2024 data, here are the average life expectancies — we use this to calculate how many years your retirement fund must cover.
stepGender.source: Source: Ministry of Interior Statistics, Taiwan Life Tables 2024
stepGender.maleTagline: Taiwan male average lifespan: 77.42 years, 6.7 years above global average 🌏
stepGender.femaleTagline: Taiwan female average lifespan: 84.30 years, 8.3 years above global average 🌸
stepGender.conceptBody: Life expectancy at a given age tells you how many more years a person can expect to live. By using "average lifespan − planned retirement age", we get a realistic retirement duration instead of assuming an infinite horizon — making your target amount more accurate.

stepAge.title: Let's Start with Time
stepAge.retireAge: At what age do you plan to retire?
stepAge.yearsToRetire: {years} years for compound interest to work for you 🚀
stepAge.infoContent: Knowing your age and target retirement date lets us calculate your "accumulation period" — the time compound interest gets to work for you. The earlier you start, the less you need to save each month. Einstein reportedly called compound interest "the eighth wonder of the world: he who understands it, earns it; he who doesn't, pays it."

validation.retireRequired: Please enter your expected retirement age
validation.retireRange: Retirement age must be between 30 and 100
validation.retireAfterCurrent: Retirement age must be greater than current age

stepExpense.title: What Does Your Dream Retirement Look Like?
stepExpense.monthlyExpense: Based on today's prices, how much per month would feel comfortably enough for you?
stepExpense.hint: Think in today's money — no need to adjust for inflation yourself. Assume all loans are paid off. Just food, leisure, housing, transport, and fun.
stepExpense.infoContent: The key here is "today's prices." Don't try to calculate inflation yourself — that's exactly what the next step is for! The number you enter represents your purchasing power in today's dollars. The system will automatically convert it to what you'll actually need in the year you retire. The "Replacement Ratio" concept suggests post-retirement spending is about 70-80% of pre-retirement income, but it's more accurate to start from your own ideal lifestyle.

validation.required: Please enter your ideal monthly expense
validation.min: Monthly expense should be at least NT$ 5,000
validation.max: Please enter a reasonable amount (under NT$ 1,000,000)

stepInflation.title: Inflation × 4% Rule = Your Target
stepInflation.inflationDescription: Inflation shrinks purchasing power over time. NT$ 100 today may only buy NT$ 55 worth of goods in 30 years (at 2% annual inflation). We use this to convert your current expenses into what you'll actually need at retirement.
stepInflation.annualReturnHint: This affects how much you need to save monthly. Reference: VT (Global Stock ETF) ~10% historical annual return; Taiwan 0050 ~12% historical annual return (both nominal, before inflation adjustment).
stepInflation.retirementYearsNote: 📅 Based on your life expectancy, your fund must last ~{years} years in retirement
stepInflation.futureExpense: Estimated annual expense at retirement: NT$ {amount}
stepInflation.currentSavingsHint: Any savings or investments already earmarked for retirement. With compound growth, they'll offset part of your target and reduce your required monthly savings.
stepInflation.savingsGrowthNote: ✨ Estimated value at retirement: NT$ {amount} — already deducted
stepInflation.savingsSufficient: Your existing savings already exceed the retirement target — no extra savings needed!
stepInflation.savingsSufficientHint: This is the power of compound interest: high returns over a long period can make your savings far exceed your retirement needs.
stepInflation.infoContent: Inflation is a "silent thief" that erodes purchasing power each year. The "4% Rule" comes from the 1998 Trinity Study: research showed that if you withdraw no more than 4% of your retirement fund per year (i.e., save 25× your annual expenses), your money has a 95%+ historical chance of lasting 30+ years — and may even keep growing. This assumes the retirement fund is invested in a diversified stock-bond portfolio, not just sitting in a savings account.
